clue.text: Tiny picture, it needs close scrutiny

definitions.meaning: a little photograph or engraving is a print of modest size
the fine-type terms tucked away in a contract, which you must read carefully

explanation.surface: A miniature image so small that you must peer at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a little reproduction of a picture, and the clauses in minute type that hide awkward conditions in a contract.

clue.text: Irritating choice of directions

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south, a compass direction
or is the word that offers a choice between two things
E is the abbreviation for east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone finds it annoying to be offered a choice of routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choice of directions' reads as S OR E: two compass points with the word of choice between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something painful or chafing is sore, as in a raw, aching spot.

clue.text: Melissa drifting was this perhaps

indicators.note: drifting means the letters of the name wander out of their order into a new one

explanation.surface: A woman named Melissa, wandering without direction, was presumably purposeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' rearranges the seven letters of MELISSA; the whole clue also describes the result, since someone drifting is without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting about with no goal is the very picture of purposeless behaviour.

clue.text: No great surprise for child prodigy

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'small wonder' or 'no wonder', meaning it is hardly surprising
a gifted youngster, a small marvel

explanation.surface: It hardly astonishes anyone when a precocious youngster shines.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something unsurprising, and taken literally names a small marvel, such as a precocious child.

clue.text: True existence as enjoyed by ordinary people

definitions.text: True existence as enjoyed by ordinary people

parts.words: True existence as enjoyed by ordinary people
parts.note: the everyday world as opposed to fiction, fantasy or celebrity, the way most folk actually live

explanation.surface: A description of the genuine, unglamorous life lived by most people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase contrasts the actual world with films, dreams or the bubble of the famous, where ordinary folk spend their days.

clue.text: Guilty of not having any American money

parts.note: no means none at all
a cent is a small coin of US currency

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being penniless in dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare legal-sounding word, the opposite of innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocent is an archaic word for culpable or harmful, the counterpart of innocent.

clue.text: Bit of a rash position

definitions.meaning: a single pimple or red mark in an outbreak on the skin
a place or location, as in a nice picnic site

explanation.surface: Someone's reckless choice of place, or a mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is one blemish of a rash, and a particular place or location is also called this.

clue.text: King or emperor, perhaps

parts.note: reads as a monarch, but King and Emperor are both species names of the flightless Antarctic seabird

explanation.surface: A guess at the rank of some royal ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'King' suggests royalty; both words actually name kinds of flightless black-and-white seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: King and emperor are two species of the flightless swimming bird of the Southern Hemisphere.

clue.text: Exchange bike during fluctuations in economic activity

parts.note: to exchange goods is to trade
a bike is a cycle

explanation.surface: Swapping bicycles during the ups and downs of the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use the phrase for the recurring pattern of boom and slump in business activity.

clue.text: It is sent to satisfy one's creditors

definitions.text: It is sent to satisfy one's creditors

parts.words: It is sent to satisfy one's creditors
parts.note: a sum of money posted off to settle a debt

explanation.surface: A payment posted to keep the people one owes happy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum of money transmitted as payment, especially to settle what is owed.

clue.text: Returnable old Indian money

indicators.note: returnable says the word reads the same when turned back to front

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An old Indian coin that can be handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returnable' sounds like a deposit on a bottle; it says the answer is the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a coin of British India worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Consider smut could have been taken the wrong way

indicators.note: could have been signals that the letters of the two words might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their words were wrongly thought to be smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could have been' rearranges the twelve letters of CONSIDER and SMUT.
explanation.definitionFit: If remarks are misinterpreted, they are understood in a sense other than the intended one.

clue.text: Close main line

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean

explanation.surface: Shutting off the principal railway route.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut something tight is to make it airtight or fasten it, as with an envelope.

clue.text: Its lines run between poles

parts.note: reads like telegraph wires strung between posts, but means meridians on a globe running from North to South Pole

explanation.surface: Telephone or telegraph wires strung from post to post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poles' suggests wooden posts carrying wires; here they are the North and South Poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Meridians are the angular measure east or west, drawn as lines from one pole of the Earth to the other.

clue.text: Cricketer not on top

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
a spinning top is a toy also called a spinner

explanation.surface: A player who is not at the peak of their form.
explanation.walkthrough: An off spinner is a cricket bowler who turns the ball from the off side; 'top' is the child's spinning toy, not a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler in cricket who makes the ball turn from off to leg is called this.

clue.text: Provided we went round swimmer first, noisy woman appeared

indicators.note: first says this piece comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: a fish is a creature that swims

indicators.note: went round says the two letters of 'we' enclose the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
provided means if, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: A shrill woman turned up once we had walked around a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went round' puts IF inside WE to make WIFE; 'first' puts the swimmer ahead of it. A fishwife was a woman selling fish, proverbially loud-mouthed.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means a coarse, loud-voiced woman, after the market women who shouted their wares.

clue.text: Have power in dirty place that is barely sufficient

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a filthy pigpen or squalid room
can means to be able to

explanation.surface: Wielding authority in a grimy spot that barely meets needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A meagre or skimpy amount is only just enough.

clue.text: Confident birds on the water

parts.note: cocks are male birds
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Male birds floating confidently on a river or lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the birds above the river; the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overconfident or arrogantly sure of oneself is the sense here.

clue.text: Back in a moment

definitions.meaning: to support a proposal or candidate
a very short time, a sixtieth of a minute

explanation.surface: Someone promises they will return shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a motion is to back it, and a very brief instant is also this word.

clue.text: Sarcastic clip

definitions.meaning: hurtful or biting, as in a remark
a press clipping, an item snipped from a newspaper

explanation.surface: A snide remark, or a piece of film.
explanation.definitionFit: A wounding remark is called biting, and an item clipped from a newspaper is also this.

clue.text: Ruin of large number about now and three months later

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the word now are turned around into a different order

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn, the season after summer

explanation.surface: Many people are ruined now and again a quarter-year later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NOW into OWN. 'three months later' presumes the puzzle appeared in summer, so the next season, autumn or fall, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse or undoing, such as the fall of a regime, is ruin.

clue.text: Sailor Stanley accepting one will not vote

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: accepting says the short name takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Stan is the short form of the name Stanley
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor called Stanley, taking someone aboard, declines to cast a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from casting a ballot is to decline formally to take part in it.

clue.text: Allowed to go round one chop initially using knife

indicators.note: to go round says the first piece surrounds the others

parts.note: to let is to permit
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word chop

explanation.surface: Permission given to hack around with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts AN plus C (first letter of 'chop') inside LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small double-edged blade is a lancet.

clue.text: Lacking information at night perhaps

definitions.meaning: literally without light, as after sunset

explanation.surface: Ignorant of the facts, or out after dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means uninformed, and literally it means without light, as at nighttime.

clue.text: What sea may do to ship

definitions.text: What sea may do to ship

parts.words: What sea may do to ship
parts.note: rough waves fling a vessel up and down

explanation.surface: The way rough waves treat a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy seas throw a boat about, pitching and rolling it.

clue.text: Some sudden earthy sandy tract

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A patch of gritty land suddenly shows earthiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of 'sudden earthy'. A dene is a sandy area near the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Dene is a dialect word for a low sandhill or dune area by the coast.

clue.text: Unsophisticated? Not applicable to one fellow

parts.note: NA is the standard abbreviation on forms for not applicable
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A form question asking whether something is irrelevant to a single man.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive, artless, and lacking worldliness: the French-derived word for innocent.

clue.text: Get together to create a fortune perhaps

definitions.text: Get together to create a fortune perhaps

parts.words: Get together to create a fortune perhaps
parts.note: gather or pile up, as wealth amassed bit by bit

explanation.surface: People joining forces to make a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get together' suggests a meeting of people; here it means gathering money until it grows large.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass or gather things over time, such as savings building up into wealth.

clue.text: Latest sort of gear

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters of the word gear are sorted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The newest kind of equipment or clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GEAR. 'All the rage' means highly fashionable, hence latest.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze or fashion, the newest thing everyone wants, is the rage.

clue.text: Those present at specified time in evening move in time to music

parts.note: ten o'clock is a time in the evening
to dance is to move rhythmically to music

explanation.surface: People who turned up at a set hour in the evening to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of people turning up at an event, the audience or turnout.
